doc: Watching one route at one pole, as a board that outlives the screen it was made on (`proposals/07`). Two rules and one clock. `watchView` composes the pill and its card out of words that already exist and are already pinned elsewhere — `routeStopBoard`, `routeStopEta`, `remarkView`, `feedNotice`, `walkMinutes`, `displayName` — so what these rows pin is the JOINS: which arm a board is in and in what order (ADR-088: pending -> unavailable -> reading -> noService, because a board on its way must never read as nothing due and a board that refused us is not an empty one), which single sentence the pill has room for when several are true at once (offline first, then the refusal, then nothing-due, then the honesty cue that the lead figure is a timetable rather than a sighting), when 'leave in N min' may be said at all, and whether the screen underneath is already drawing this very board. `watchExpired` is the clock: a watch outlives the RIDER's last touch by 90 minutes, never the data's — a watch holds an open subscription, so ageing it on arriving rounds would mean it never expires at all. THE PAYLOADS ARE HAND-BUILT TO THE WIRE SHAPE rather than trimmed from a dataset extract, which is a departure from this package's other corpora and is stated rather than hidden: a watch's inputs are one `EtaReport` plus a record the rider made, and the record has no upstream to be extracted from. Every id is shaped like the dataset's, every name is the real bilingual name of a real KMB 1 pole, and every reading is re-timed against a fixed `now` of 2026-09-20T09:00:00+08:00 so that no row reads a clock. No row here is `knownDefect`.

watchExpired.doc: 90 minutes from the rider's last touch, boundary pinned from both sides, and an unreadable timestamp expiring rather than living for ever. The TTL is an argument so a caller — a test today, a setting later — can say how long a journey is.

cases.name: inside-the-window
cases.why: Eight minutes after the rider last touched it — the ordinary case, and the one a pill is drawn for.

cases.name: the-last-minute-inside
cases.why: Exactly 90 minutes is NOT expired: the comparison is strictly greater, so the boundary belongs to the rider.

cases.name: one-second-past
cases.why: A second later it is gone. The pair pins the boundary from both sides, which is where a port fabricates an off-by-one.

cases.name: an-unreadable-timestamp-expires
cases.why: Fail towards forgetting: a watch that cannot be aged would hold a subscription open for ever. Losing it costs one tap.

cases.name: a-caller-may-shorten-the-window
cases.why: The TTL is an argument, not a constant read from inside — so a test, and a future setting, can say how long a journey is.

watchView.doc: The pill and its card: four readout arms in ADR-088's order, a note whose precedence is the only genuinely new decision in the module, the walk arithmetic behind 'leave in N min' (including the two rows where the honest answer is no line at all), the redundancy test a renderer is forbidden to make for itself, and the bilingual read of the labels the rider's watch carries.

cases.name: a-board-with-times-leads-with-the-first
cases.why: The ordinary arm. The lead is the pill’s figure and the rest is what the card adds, so one board is split once rather than by each renderer.

cases.name: no-round-has-landed-yet
cases.why: ADR-088’s first arm: a board on its way must never render as “nothing due”. `pending` is what a skeleton is drawn from.

cases.name: a-board-that-refused-is-not-an-empty-board
cases.why: ADR-073/077. The pole is named in `failed`, so the readout is `unavailable` and the note is a warning — never “no service”.

cases.name: answered-and-nothing-is-due
cases.why: The only arm that may say “no service”: we asked, we were answered, and the answer was nothing. Reached only after `failed` is ruled out.

cases.name: offline-outranks-every-other-sentence
cases.why: The note’s precedence, top entry: a rider whose network is gone needs that before anything it might explain. The readings stay — ADR-058 replays them aged rather than blanking the pill.

cases.name: a-timetable-is-not-a-sighting
cases.why: The honesty cue the pill has room for: `remarkKind: scheduled` means the figure is the published timetable, not a bus anyone has seen (ADR-008). Muted, because nothing is wrong — it is simply a weaker claim.

cases.name: leave-in-subtracts-the-walk-from-the-lead
cases.why: P13, finally answerable: 320 m is a 4 min walk and the lead is 11 min away, so the rider has 7 min. The subtraction is the kernel’s because two renderers would round it differently.

cases.name: leave-now-when-the-walk-exactly-fills-the-wait
cases.why: Zero is kept and means *leave now* — the boundary between a line worth printing and a false reassurance.

cases.name: a-bus-you-cannot-catch-says-nothing
cases.why: The lead is 3 min away and the rider is a 10 min walk from the kerb. Flooring at zero would print “leave now” to someone who cannot make it; the honest answer is no line at all.

cases.name: due-has-no-minutes-to-subtract
cases.why: Falls out of the arithmetic rather than needing an arm: `Due` is 0 minutes and the walk floor is 1, so the leave line is absent without a special case.

cases.name: the-screen-underneath-is-already-showing-this-board
cases.why: A route screen at this pole and this route. The comparison is the kernel’s because comparing ids in a view is the derivation `check-no-derivation` bans.

cases.name: a-place-screen-names-no-route-and-still-shows-this-one
cases.why: Place detail draws every route at the pole, so a `showing` with no route is redundant too — the asymmetry that would otherwise be re-derived per screen.

cases.name: another-route-at-the-same-pole-is-not-redundant
cases.why: Same kerb, different board. Without the route half of the test the pill would hide itself while showing something the screen does not.

cases.name: the-names-are-read-in-the-riders-language
cases.why: The captured labels are `I18nText`, so switching language re-reads them with no fetch — and `displayName` splits the printed code off the Chinese name exactly as it does the English one (ADR-034).

cases.name: a-stale-board-still-reads-out-and-says-so
cases.why: The board is 20 minutes old: the readings stand — aged, never hidden — and the sentence is `feedNotice`’s, at screen level, because staleness is the board’s and not a mark on a figure (ADR-123/133).

cases.name: a-lone-pole-has-no-stand-to-name
cases.why: ADR-080's line exists to tell two kerbs a metre apart apart, so a stop with one kerb has nothing to say and says nothing — `null`, never an empty string a renderer would draw a blank row for.
